evidence.quoted_text:
for (const [key, value] of updates) {
    if (!object.has(key)) entries.push([key, value]);
evidence.reason: `withObjectKeys` builds `replacement` as a `Map`, so repeated updates to the same new key are deduplicated with the final value, but the append loop iterates the original `updates` array and checks only `object.has(key)`. For an empty object with updates `[["x", 1], ["x", 2]]`, it appends both `x` entries; `JsonObject.get("x")` then returns the first value `1` instead of the final assigned value `2`. This violates the documented Python assignment/setdefault semantics. Iterating `replacement` instead keeps the first insertion position and applies the final value once.
